To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and characterized species-specific third generation recombinant Ah receptor-responsive CALUX cell bioassay with significantly improved detection limit, increased response to 2,3-7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p- dioxin and enhanced detection of dioxin-like and other Ah receptor agonists.
we developed species-specific third generation CALUX cell lines that exhibit significantly improved detection limits and dramatically increased induction response to dioxin-like chemicals.
we developed species-specific G3 CALUX (chemiluminescent reporter gene assay) cell bioassays with improved detection limits and significantly enhanced responses to dioxin-like contaminants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new CALUX cell lines with improved detection limits for screening samples for the presence or absence of AhR agonist compounds and dioxin-like chemicals.

the development and application of novel AhR-responsive CALIX cell lines for the detection of AhR agonist/antagonist activity and the development of new methods for the detection of DLCs in complex environmental samples.

the development of novel, highly sensitive and species-specific AhR responsive G3 CALUX cells that will improve our ability to detect and identify dioxin-like chemicals and AhR agonist/antagonist activity in environmental samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the development of species-specific G2/G3 CALUX cell bioassay will facilitate the detection of dioxin and dioxin-like compound contamination at lower levels than currently possible with existing CALUX cell lines.

the G3 CALUX bioassays are a useful and reliable tool for screening of environmental matrices for the presence of dioxin-like contaminants and AhR agonist/antagonists, especially in samples with low contamination levels.

the new G3 cell lines are more sensitive and responsive compared to the existing AhR-Calux cell bioassays, and therefore are a more suitable cell line for screening samples for the presence or absence of dioxin and dioxin-like chemicals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully generated species-specific third generation recombinant Ah receptor (Ah-R) responsive luciferase reporter cell lines with significantly improved sensitivity and response to 2,3',7,8-tetra-chlorodibenzo-1,4-p-dioxin, dioxin-like chemicals, and other Ah-R agonists.
we have developed a novel G3 AhR-responsive CALUC cell line with a significantly improved limit of TCDD detection and enhanced response to AhR agonists.

the G3 cells are more sensitive and more specific to TCDD and related compounds than other cell lines and are the most sensitive cell line to date for detection of dioxins and dioxin-like chemicals in environmental samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to develop species-specific G3 AhR CALUX cell lines, and that these new cell lines have significantly improved detection limits and induction responses compared to existing Ah-responsive CALUX cell bioassay cell lines.

the G3 CALUX cells have significantly enhanced sensitivity and responsiveness to TCDD and other AhR agonists, which should facilitate the use of the G3 CALUC cell bioassay for screening of samples for AhR agonists and DLCs.
we have developed a novel species-specific G3 AhR-CALUV cell bioassay for screening samples for the presence AhR agonists and/or antagonists.
